labels.matrixDescription: Current official AI client support matrix for the UnlimGPT CLI.
labels.cliDescription: Command reference for the published @unlimgpt/cli package.
labels.cliInstallNotice: Install the [published @unlimgpt/cli package](/docs/cli/install). Before using a command, check your installed version with `unlimgpt --version` and available commands with `unlimgpt --help`: this reference may describe a newer release.
labels.diagnostic: If the request fails, run `unlimgpt doctor --client {clientId}` and see [troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/doctor). Diagnostics do not replace a real request.
labels.verificationExample: This launch check requires Python 3 and makes one billable request through the child process environment. If `gpt-5.6-sol` is unavailable to your key, use an accessible model ID from the catalog; the secret does not appear in command arguments.

prerequisites: Setup signs you in and creates an API key if needed; the secret stays in the operating-system credential store.
rotate: Record the old key ID from `unlimgpt keys list`, then create and select a new key with `unlimgpt keys create --name codex-next`.
Send a request in Codex and confirm it in [API Activity](/api-activity); restart Codex if needed. Revoke the old key only after a successful request.
revoke: Revoke a key on the [API keys page](/api-keys) after confirming the new connection; the old key immediately loses access.
revert: Run the exact command printed after `Undo:` by `configure`. The CLI leaves later third-party edits intact.
codex.title: Codex CLI
codex.summary: Automatic Codex CLI 0.156.1 setup for GPT-6 Sol.
setup: Configure Codex CLI 0.156.1 with `gpt-6-sol`. This command does not yet support other models.
Preview the fields that would change, without writing: `unlimgpt configure codex --dry-run`.
Quit Codex Desktop. If previous sessions exist, after writing `config.toml` the CLI creates a backup of Codex session stores in its `backups` directory; it includes chat content. Keep it private.
Apply the owned block: `unlimgpt configure codex`.
The CLI adds the `unlimgpt` provider; the secret stays in the OS credential store and is returned through `auth.command`.
verify: Reopen Codex Desktop and confirm your previous chats are still visible.
Start a new Codex chat, send “Reply with READY”, wait for a non-empty response, and confirm the request in [API Activity](/api-activity). The wording may vary; the request uses credits.

troubleshooting.resolution: Upgrade to a Codex release with native provider auth commands; plaintext fallback is intentionally unavailable.
Inspect the effective user-level `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`, then rerun `unlimgpt configure codex`.

uninstall: Run the guarded receipt revert, then revoke the dedicated Codex key if no other client uses it.

claude-code.title: Claude Code
claude-code.summary: Automatic setup through the official `apiKeyHelper` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` surfaces.
setup: Review precedence and the fields that would change: `unlimgpt configure claude-code --dry-run`.
Apply the configuration: `unlimgpt configure claude-code`.
The CLI never writes the key to JSON; Claude Code obtains it through `apiKeyHelper`.
verify: Open Claude Code, send “Reply with READY”, wait for a non-empty response, and confirm the request in [API Activity](/api-activity). The wording may vary; the request uses credits.

troubleshooting.resolution: Remove a higher-precedence `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, then rerun doctor.
Contact your administrator; the CLI does not bypass managed policy.

uninstall: Run the guarded receipt revert, then revoke the dedicated Claude Code key.

continue.title: Continue CLI
continue.summary: Secret-free model configuration plus ephemeral environment injection through the secure launcher.
setup: Preview the YAML fields that would change: `unlimgpt configure continue --dry-run`.
Apply it: `unlimgpt configure continue`.
Start the CLI with `unlimgpt launch continue -- cn --config ~/.continue/config.yaml`; configure the IDE extension separately through its native secret UI.
verify: Run `unlimgpt launch continue -- cn --config ~/.continue/config.yaml`. If you configured `--profile work`, use `unlimgpt launch continue --profile work -- cn --config ~/.continue/config.yaml` with your actual profile name. The `--config` flag opens the local YAML even when a different config was previously selected. In Continue CLI, use `/model` to select the UnlimGPT model, send “Reply with READY”, wait for a non-empty response, and confirm the request in [API Activity](/api-activity). The wording may vary; the request uses credits.

troubleshooting.problem: The YAML uses anchors or directives.
troubleshooting.resolution: The CLI stops before writing; use guided setup so YAML semantics are preserved.

troubleshooting.problem: The IDE cannot read the shell variable.
troubleshooting.resolution: That is expected for the extension: use Continue's native UI/Hub instead of a plaintext `.env`.

uninstall: Run the guarded revert and remove the native Continue secret if you created one for the IDE.

prerequisites: Install Cursor and confirm it offers an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and API key field.
rotate: Record the old key ID from `unlimgpt keys list`, create a new key with `unlimgpt keys create --name cursor-next`, then rerun `unlimgpt configure cursor` to copy the new key.
Paste it into Cursor's native secret field. Send a real request in Cursor and confirm it in [API Activity](/api-activity); only then revoke the old key on the API keys page.
revoke: Revoke a key on the [API keys page](/api-keys) after confirming the new connection; the old key immediately loses access.
revert: The CLI did not modify Cursor; remove the key and model through its UI.
cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.summary: Guided setup through Cursor's documented UI; the extension's internal secret storage is never modified.
setup: Run `unlimgpt configure cursor` and open Settings → Models → API Keys.
Test Cursor Local IDE in Ask first: Agent with a custom OpenAI endpoint is not guaranteed; Cloud Agents do not use BYOK keys.
Enable Use OpenAI API Key and Override OpenAI Base URL; enter the exact model ID without a prefix.

To choose effort from Cursor's model picker, append `-effort-low` and `-effort-high` to the model ID shown by the CLI through Add Custom Model. For example: `gpt-6-sol-effort-low` and `gpt-6-sol-effort-high`.
Cursor's separate Reasoning control may omit reasoning_effort on a custom Base URL; choose the corresponding model entry.
Copy the displayed Base URL and model ID. The CLI temporarily copies the API key to the clipboard.
Paste the API key from the clipboard only into Cursor's native secret field; the CLI never reads SQLite or VS Code SecretStorage.
verify: Open Cursor, send “Reply with READY” through the configured model, wait for a non-empty response, and confirm the request in [API Activity](/api-activity). The wording may vary; the request uses credits.

troubleshooting.problem: There is no custom endpoint field.
troubleshooting.resolution: Upgrade Cursor and select its official OpenAI-compatible provider; the CLI does not automate hidden internal formats.
Verify the selected provider, Base URL, and model id, then run doctor.

uninstall: Remove the UnlimGPT profile and secret through Cursor's UI, then revoke the dedicated API key.

generic-openai.title: OpenAI-compatible client
generic-openai.summary: Securely launch an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible client without writing a secret to config or shell history.
setup: Run `unlimgpt configure generic-openai` to prepare the profile and key.
Start your chosen program through `unlimgpt launch openai`: after `--`, supply its installed executable name and normal arguments. Only the child process receives the Base URL and key.
If you configured a separate profile such as `work`, add `--profile work` before `--` when launching; this uses that profile's key without changing the active profile.
verify: Send “Reply with READY” in the launched OpenAI-compatible client, wait for a non-empty response, and confirm the request in [API Activity](/api-activity). The wording may vary; the request uses credits.
If you configured `--profile work`, add the same flag before `--` in the runnable example below, using your actual profile name; otherwise it uses the active profile's key.

troubleshooting.resolution: Use its documented custom endpoint/secret UI or a dedicated guided adapter.

uninstall: Stop using the launcher and revoke the dedicated key; no configuration file was created.

setup: Run `unlimgpt configure generic-anthropic` to prepare the profile and key.
Start your chosen program through `unlimgpt launch anthropic`: after `--`, supply its installed executable name and normal arguments. The key is never written to a shell profile.
If you configured a separate profile such as `work`, add `--profile work` before `--` when launching; this uses that profile's key without changing the active profile.
verify: Send “Reply with READY” in the launched Anthropic-compatible client, wait for a non-empty response, and confirm the request in [API Activity](/api-activity). The wording may vary; the request uses credits.

troubleshooting.resolution: Use its documented endpoint/secret mechanism; never move the key into argv.

commands.login: Sign in by approving a device code in your browser.
commands.logout: Revoke the CLI OAuth session and remove its local refresh token.
commands.whoami: Inspect the current user and organization.
commands.models: List every available model and its capabilities.
commands.organizations: List your organizations or select an organization for the current profile.
commands.keys: Manage API keys for the current organization. `keys permissions <key-id> --scope models:read --scope inference:write` replaces the permission set; `--clear` removes both permissions and `--json` returns safe metadata. `keys spend-limit <key-id> --micro-credits <amount>` sets the total key budget: 0 denies new spending and `--clear` removes the cap without resetting spent credits.
commands.configure: Configure a client or show manual steps; `cloud` and `claude` alias `claude-code`.
commands.revert: Revert an owned change when the file has not changed since setup.
commands.doctor: Run free diagnostics; the paid probe requires explicit opt-in.
commands.update: Show the published version. With --yes, npm installs that exact release and leaves profiles, sign-in and API keys in place.
commands.credential: Return a key only to a native credential helper through stdout.
commands.launch: Launch a child process with an ephemeral secret environment; `--profile` selects a saved profile without changing the active one.
commands.clients: Show the current client support matrix.
